entries.title: Coverage maps: build them, keep them fresh, and cut the test suite with them
entries.body:
Builds the first full set of coverage maps, settles how they are kept fresh, and uses them to cut the test suite:
cut existing redundant tests, and scope the verify gate to the tests that cover a diff.

entries.title: Decide how the coverage maps are kept fresh: triggers, batch, staleness and sharing across machines
entries.body:
## Seen (orch, 2026-11-09)

The coverage maps exist as code since project `redundancy-check` landed, but how they are kept fresh was settled piecemeal:

- The prime dobby starts `lym gate testmap --max <test_map_batch>` (default 5) after every `test_map_every` (default 5) landings, and nothing else starts one.
- A map is stale when its package's Go files at HEAD changed, when it is older than `test_map_max_age_days` (7), or when it records a failed build at another HEAD.
  A change to a dependency, or to a non-Go file of the package, does not mark it stale; only the age limit bounds that drift.
- A stale package's map is rebuilt whole: `internal/testcover` builds a coverage binary and runs every top-level test alone, serially, one process per test.
  Per-test coverage needs that, since coverage counters are process-wide and tests run in parallel in one process mix their counts,
  so an ordinary gate run of the package cannot update its map.
- The maps live under `_bolt/.lym/testcover`, which git excludes, so each machine builds and keeps its own set:
  a move to another machine, by `lym adopt` or otherwise, starts from no maps.
- A refresh holds a gate slot while it builds, so runs' gates wait behind it.

The operator finds keeping the maps fresh this way too large a job to run again and again.

## Proposal (orch)

1. Update a map in part instead of rebuilding it whole.
   A map keys blocks by content and carries each test's source hash, so after a change only these tests need to run again:
   a test that is new or whose source changed, and a test whose recorded blocks include a block that changed or was removed.
   A test that touched none of the changed code takes the same path as before.
   After a landing that is usually a handful of tests, not the package.
2. A stale or missing map never gives a wrong answer, only a slower gate:
   a gate that scopes by the maps runs the whole package when its map is missing or stale.
   That makes a lagging map harmless, so upkeep can run lazily.
3. Build when the machine is idle, with no gate waiting, rather than holding gate slots while runs work.
4. Drop or lengthen the weekly age rebuild: with item 2, dependency drift costs only scope, not correctness.
   A change in a package this package imports can still change a test's path without changing the package; decide whether that needs more than the age limit.
5. Share the maps across machines, for instance through the Bolt checkout or the records branch:
   they are keyed by content, not by machine, so each map is built once in all.
6. Cutting existing redundant tests (`redundancy-sweep-existing`) is a one-off that needs fresh maps only when it runs;
   only gate scoping (`gate-scope-by-coverage-map`) needs maps kept fresh.

Note `testmap-backlog-drain` is one part of the trigger question; this note owns the whole policy.

## Research first

Before the design, three agents brainstorm, each on its own and without seeing the others' answers,
whether there is a smarter way to keep per-test coverage maps fresh:
Fable, Codex astra, and Opus at high effort.
Each reads `internal/testcover`, `internal/gatecli/testmap.go`, the prime dobby's refresh step and this note, and writes its own proposal.
One brainstorm per agent, three in all.
The proposals land together in one report under `docs/research/`, compared side by side, as the input for the design.
Codex fails on OSL-1046 for its bubblewrap sandbox, so the research runs on Neve.

entries.title: creel post to a strand that is not running reports plain success
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #96](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/96).

## Seen

After a machine crash, the hub prime's orch (`dop:orch`) was not running: `lym reed list` showed it `live: false`.
A beam orch posted it a request with `lym creel post dop:orch "<text>"`.
The command printed only `{"id":224,"ok":true,"sender":"..."}`, with no word that the recipient was down.
The sender told the operator the request was on its way, and the operator found the recipient dead only by asking.

## Workaround

Check `lym reed list` (or the session list) for the recipient's `live` flag before relying on a post, and ask the operator to start it.

## Expected

`creel post` to a strand that is not live still queues the message, but says so in its output, for example a `recipient_live: false` field and a warning line naming the strand and how to start it (`lym beam start` for an orch).

entries.title: Webster amends a card commit it already pushed, so the task branch diverges from origin
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #97](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/97).

## Seen

In tapestry run `models-backend` (DrillOpPlan hub), Webster committed card 3 as `8cbbf19` ("3: models-simulator") and pushed it at 08:43:57, then started the card's `lym gate card-verify` (a long tier).
After the verify, the fixes were folded into the same card commit by amending it: local `1a8de1d` ("3: models-simulator", 09:14:55), same parent `fc7e5f2`.
The next push found the branch diverged (ahead 1, behind 1), and batten stopped Run-Shed with a question to the parent offering merge, force-push or reset.
The run had a machine crash and a `lym loom resume` earlier the same morning; it is unclear whether the amend comes from the resume path or from Webster's normal verify-fix path.

## Workaround

The parent compared the two commits (`1a8de1d` = `8cbbf19` plus the verify fixes), force-pushed with `git push --force-with-lease=hanf/models-backend:8cbbf19 origin hanf/models-backend`, and resumed with `lym batten run models-backend`.

## Expected

A card commit that has been pushed is never amended: verify fixes land as a new commit, or the push waits until the card's verify passes.
Failing that, batten recognises an amended copy of the same card commit (same parent, same subject, local a superset) and settles the divergence itself with a leased force-push instead of stopping the run.

entries.title: config: per-machine or per-user branch_prefix, and a review of other per-user keys
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #99](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/99).

## What was seen

`fabric.branch_prefix` can be set only on the hub's default layer, which is committed in the board repository and applies to every machine and user of the hub.
`lym config fabric --layer machine --set branch_prefix=x/` is refused with "fabric has no machine key",
and `--layer local` is refused with "key branch_prefix is cross-pair and cannot be set in a local override".

A branch prefix usually names the person who owns the branches, such as `<user>/<slug>`.
On a hub shared by several people, or one person on several machines with different conventions, one hub-wide value does not fit.

## Idea

- Let `branch_prefix` be set per machine, or per user, with the hub default as the fallback.
  Since #59, teardown uses the recorded branch name, so a pair's branch no longer depends on the prefix in force later; a pair created on one machine keeps its name when adopted on another.
- Review which other keys are personal rather than hub-wide and give them the same layer, for example:
  the identity a pull request is opened under or assigned to, the Slack operator, the default model or effort a session opens with, and editor or window settings such as `batten.open_ide`.

entries.title: Finalize spawns a fixer on a single non-repeating test failure
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #100](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/100).

## What was seen

A beam's Finalize landing ran the gate (tier0 and tier1) on the beam head.
One tier0 test of 3463 failed with `UnauthorizedAccessException`, and tier1 passed.
The test enumerates the source tree, `bin/` included, while another test running in parallel held a temporary directory under `bin/` with its read permission removed.
The failure is a race between two tests of the repository, not a fault of the change being landed.

Finalize wrote `.lym/verify/landing-failure.yaml` and spawned a fixer strand at once, on that single run.
The gate's own failure report said that no failing test or error line was read from the tier0 output, so the fixer started without a named cause.

## Workaround

The orch read the verify log, diagnosed the race and messaged the fixer with the cause.

## Expected behaviour

- Before Finalize spawns a fixer, it reruns the failed tests (or the failed tier) once on the same head.
  A failure that does not repeat is recorded as flaky in the landing report, and the landing goes on.
- The gate's failure report names the failing test and its error message when the test runner printed them, instead of reporting that no failing test line was read.

entries.title: A paused Webster session acts on a decision notice without the run lock, and the loom row stays blocked
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #101](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/101).

## What happened

A tapestry run's Webster paused on the parent's order: Webster wrote `outcome: stuck`, the loom row went to `blocked · Webster`, and the outer batten driver yielded.
The Webster session itself stayed open: its strand (`<hub>:<task>:webster`) was still live in `lym reed list`.

Later the parent recorded a decision on the run with `lym loom decision add <slug> --by parent`.
That verb notified the live Webster strand (`"notified":["<hub>:<task>:webster"]`).
The idle Webster session woke on that notice and went on working in the old session, outside any `lym webster run`:
it forked the batch, merged, committed two cards, ran the verify gate and wrote `outcome.yaml` with `outcome: done`.
`record-batch` warned that no live `lym webster run` owned the state, because the session was not started under the run's lock.

## Result

`lym webster status` showed every batch done, but the loom row stayed `blocked` at Webster with the old pause reason, and `lym batten status` showed `failed` with `battencli: cannot resume`.
`lym batten run <slug>` yielded with the stale blocked error.
The overview page showed the tapestry as blocked although its work was done.
Running `lym loom resume` in the task worktree was needed to get the driver to re-run Webster and move on.
Meanwhile the parent's own `lym webster run` would have started a second Webster beside the lockless one.

## Expected

A Webster that reports stuck ends its session, or a session that does not hold the run's lock refuses to act on mail and says so.
`lym loom decision add` does not wake a producer strand whose run is halted, or warns the parent that it did.
`record-batch` without the lock refuses rather than warns, so the work and the loom row cannot drift apart.

entries.title: heddle set/remove should re-render file targets in every live worktree of the hub
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #103](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/103).

lym heddle set and lym heddle remove save the entry and render HEDDLE.md, but leave every existing worktree's rendered files (CLAUDE.local.md, AGENTS.override.md, .claude/settings.local.json) stale until the worktree is made, taken in, or rendered by hand with lym heddle render.

Seen: a new repository entry with target claude-file was set from a beam worktree. CLAUDE.local.md in that worktree, in the prime worktree and in a running task worktree all lacked the entry until lym heddle render was run in each one by hand.

An instruction entry usually exists because agents must follow it now (for example, a module that is out of scope), so agents in running task worktrees keep working without it, and nothing tells the caller which worktrees are stale.

Proposal: after a successful set or remove, render every file target into every live code worktree of the hub (prime, beams, task pairs), and report the rendered and failed worktrees in the verb's output. Running Claude sessions then take the change at their next compaction, as today; an optional flag to skip the fan-out could cover bulk edits.

entries.title: heddle file targets: split claude-file and codex-file, add a shared target for both
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #104](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/104).

A heddle entry with target claude-file is rendered into both CLAUDE.local.md (Claude Code) and AGENTS.override.md (Codex). The name says Claude only, and there is no way to give an instruction to one agent family alone, although some instructions apply to Codex and not to Claude, or the other way round.

Proposal: three file targets.

- claude-file renders into CLAUDE.local.md only.
- codex-file renders into AGENTS.override.md only.
- A new shared target (for example agents-file) renders into both.

Existing claude-file entries keep today's behaviour by migrating to the shared target. lym heddle set --help, lym heddle list and HEDDLE.md state which files each file target renders to.

entries.title: gate test: card gate and explicit target never reach a second test project when tier0 command lacks a targets placeholder
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #105](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/105).

## What happened

A card created tests in a second test project (a slow-tests project), but the hub's tier0 command runs only the fast test assembly, and tier1 is empty.
`lym gate test --gate card --card <card>`, the batch gate, and an explicit `lym gate test <project> -- --filter ...` all ran the fast suite instead.
The tier0 command holds neither `{targets}` nor `{test_targets}`, so the requested target was silently ignored.
The card was committed after only a compile check of the slow-tests project; its tests never ran through any gate route.
The tests were later found failing only because an agent ran them through `lym gate test --tier 1 --card <card> -- --filter ...` by hand.

## Why it is abnormal

A gate that is asked for a named target and cannot pass it to the command reports a pass for different tests, with no warning.
A card whose tests live outside the configured tier0 assembly gets no verification and nothing says so.

## What to do

- Refuse or warn when a gate or explicit target is requested and the tier command has no `{targets}` or `{test_targets}` placeholder.
- Warn when a card adds or edits tests in a project that no configured tier command reaches.

Provenance: task `trip-history-transfer`; notes `04-aligner-moving-junction-recovery.md`, `04-aligner-moving-junction.md`.

entries.title: loom halt: 'verify gate failed after 4 attempt(s) of 3: none named' reports an off-by-one count and no failure
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #106](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/106).

## What happened

`lym loom` halted blocked at the Webster row with anomaly `escalation-to-human` and the reason:

`verify gate failed after 4 attempt(s) of 3: none named`

## Why it is abnormal

- The message counts 4 attempts against a limit of 3, which reads as an off-by-one in the retry counter or its wording.
- "none named" gives no failing test, project or gate output, so the operator cannot tell what failed or whether the gate itself errored.
- The halt note offers no way forward and names only the trace file.

## What to do

- Make the attempt count and the limit agree, or state that the limit counts retries after the first attempt.
- Include the failing gate, target and the tail of its output in the halt reason, and say explicitly when the gate produced no failure to name.
- Add a way-forward line, as other halt reasons have.

Provenance: task `trip-history-transfer`; note `loom-halt.md`.

entries.title: Dobby starts a released raddle task whose depends_on has not landed
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #107](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/107).

## What happened

In a beam, the orch promoted a Sketch with `lym board promote S1`, which made it a task with recipe `raddle`.
It then ran `lym board set-deps '{"slug":"<slug>","depends_on":["<other>"]}'`, where `<other>` was a task of the same beam still `running · PR-Review`, and only after that released the task with `lym board set-status '{"slug":"<slug>","status":null}'`.
`lym board get` showed `depends_on` set and the status already `running · Seed-Child` moments later: the beam's dobby started the raddle task although its dependency had not landed.

## Workaround

`lym batten pause <slug>` holds the run; the orch resumes it with `lym batten run <slug>` once the dependency lands.

## Expected

Dobby starts a released task only when every entry in its `depends_on` is done or gone, whatever its recipe, `raddle` included.

entries.title: Worktree-Create halts on a reused slug path holding only obj/ leftovers
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #108](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/108).

Seen: `lym beam merge-parent support-for-dop` halted its batten run at Worktree-Create because the directory `<hub>/support-for-dop-merge-in` already existed and was not a worktree.
It held only `src/csharp/NORCE.Models/*/obj/Debug/...` build leftovers (15 files, generated AssemblyInfo and editorconfig) dated from the previous merge-in run of the same slug a day earlier, which had landed and been torn down.
Something (an IDE or a build triggered after teardown) recreated obj directories under the removed worktree path, and Worktree-Teardown does not check for or clean such leftovers.

Workaround: inspected the directory, removed it by hand (`rm -r` on the literal path), and ran `lym batten run support-for-dop-merge-in` again.

Expected: a reused slug whose old path holds only build output (obj/bin) is not blocked; Worktree-Create, or Worktree-Teardown of the earlier run, removes a directory that contains nothing but build artefacts, or the halt names it as such so the parent does not need to inspect it.

entries.title: The hub workspace file lists every pair, beams' pairs included, named with their project handle
entries.body:
## Seen (operator, 2026-11-11)

The hub workspace file `<hub>/<repo>.code-workspace` lists the prime, Bolt and every pair whose parent is the prime, beams included,
but no pair under a beam: those are only in the beam's own `<repo>-<beam>.code-workspace`.
The operator rarely opens VS Code, and when they do they want to see all of a repository's code in one window,
so a beam's tasks missing from the hub file sends them to a second window.
A folder is named by its slug alone, such as `adopt-worker-record`, so nothing shows which project it belongs to.

## Idea

- The hub workspace file lists every pair of the hub, the pairs under each beam included, at any depth.
- Each pair's folder name leads with its project's handle, `P1: adopt-worker-record`, when its board entry belongs to a project;
  a pair with no project keeps its slug alone.
  The handle comes from the board at regeneration, so a regeneration after a board change brings it current.
- The beam workspace files stay as they are.

The machine restart launcher (`machine-restart-shortcut`) opens only this hub file, so it relies on it listing every pair.
